chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from al-'Iyyas ibn al-Qasim said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performs the ritual bath for Ihram in Medina, wears two garments, and then sleeps before entering the state of Ihram. He said: 'There is no obligatory bath upon him.' Therefore, it does not contradict the two previous narrations, because he (peace be upon him) only said there is no obligatory bath, and he did not negate the bath from him as a recommended and preferred act.

key_terms.النَّدْبِ: Recommendation (a level of legal ruling below obligation)
key_terms.لِلْإِحْرَامِ: For Ihram (state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: Is it necessary to repeat the ritual bath for Ihram if one sleeps before entering the state of consecration?
ai.summary: In this narration from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the legal nuance between obligation (*fard*) and recommendation (*mustahabb*) regarding the Ihram bath after sleep. He explains that while the bath is not strictly required to be repeated, its omission does not negate its status as a recommended act, thereby preserving the virtue of the practice without imposing a burden of repetition. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly approach to differentiating between mandatory acts and those that are highly encouraged but not strictly binding in specific circumstances.
